payload.title: Sitewright
payload.seoDescription: Open infrastructure for websites your clients can update from a chat assistant. The assistant interprets intent; the infrastructure enforces the boundary.

props.title: Websites your clients update from ChatGPT.
props.lead: No admin dashboard. A request becomes a command file in Git, validated and signed before it reaches the site. The assistant interprets intent; the infrastructure enforces the boundary, and the AI is not the authority.

props.heading: The admin panel is the maintenance.

blocks.content: Traditional CMS products are not incapable. The weight is in keeping administrative software alive so that someone can change a sentence on a page.

items: Roles and permissions for people who post twice a month
Incidents in software nobody wanted to run
All of it to publish a paragraph.

props.heading: One canonical path for client changes.

blocks.content: A client sentence becomes an immutable command file. It is committed, validated, rejected if its id has been used before, dry-run, then dispatched to the Worker with an HMAC-signed request.
The site's operating history is the repository's history. Other API ingress exists for implementers and for emergencies, and each is documented.

items.title: “Replace the hero image with this photo.”
“Change our Sunday opening hours to 6 PM.”
“Update the SEO description for the About page.”

props.heading: Instruct for quality. Enforce for consequences.

blocks.content: Over four days of real operation, instructed rules were broken four times. Boundaries enforced by the application were never broken.

items: A command that fails validation is not applied.
A repeated command id applies nothing.
A version conflict stops the write.
An unauthorized scope is refused before any mutation.

blocks.content: These are not prompts. They are the application refusing.

items.label: days of real operation before release
defects and gaps found and recorded
contract checks on a clean clone
minutes from clone to a live post

props.heading: Your code. Your data. Your infrastructure.

blocks.content: Nothing runs on our account. You provision your own GitHub repository and your own Cloudflare account, and you keep them.

items: No hosted service in the path
Fork it and replace the reference design

props.heading: Which assistants can operate a site

items.question: What does an assistant need to be able to do?
items.answer: Commit a file to a GitHub repository. That is a real requirement, not a formality — not every assistant can do it today.

items.question: ChatGPT
items.answer: Verified. A real company's site was operated this way for four days, on a desktop and on a phone, for text and for images.

items.question: Claude
items.answer: Its chat interface cannot connect to GitHub today. Claude Code can, but that is a developer tool rather than something a client uses.

items.question: Is this an official OpenAI project?
items.answer: No. Sitewright is an independent open-source project, not affiliated with, endorsed by, or certified by OpenAI, xAI, Anthropic, or Google.

props.heading: Built from evidence, not from a plan.
props.body: New capability follows repeated real use. A request that appears once is recorded, not built.
